analysis:
This PR is documentation-only. It updates docs/README.md and docs/architecture/README.md to say that backend, console and admin source and operating guides belong to the platform repository. It also removes the dangling index links to the retained console snapshot, and deletes docs/architecture/components/console-ui.md. The units contain no executable code, so no runtime behavior, keys, attestation paths, provider/coordinator wire handling, cache storage or local sockets changed.

The changed text does not touch TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011 or TB-012 controls. It does not touch the T-041 prefix-cache posture (HMAC-keyed names, 30-minute TTL, account-scoped cacheSalt) or the A-008, A-015 and A-016 token/authorization handling.

One observation, not a finding: the deleted document described the console's Privy/API-key handling, CSP and mock-auth failure mode. The provider threat model scopes out the consumer console and backend (out_of_scope). The removed prose therefore does not invalidate any retained provider threat entry. The README text states that the console source ownership moved to the platform repo. The supplied evidence does not show whether console-ui/ source is also removed from this repo in the same PR, or whether other docs still link to the deleted file (for example reference/configuration.md, developer/test.md, security/encryption.md, which were not supplied). Any such dangling links would be a documentation integrity issue, not a security regression. If console code stays in this repo without its documented security invariants, that is a documentation-coverage question for later review only.

No files under provider-swift were changed, and no mitigation was weakened.
